note: MAPPING: data/hexaco_ashton_2014.r reads data.csv and pivots select(starts_with('A')) by column NAME, so the live code IS the source column name (AForg1..APati10); codebook.txt keys each of those codes to its sentence one per line ('AGent6 I am quick to judge others.'), 40/40 A-codes present, no duplicates among its 240 codes. No positional step. INSTRUMENT (Step 3b): despite the table name/description 'HEXACO Personality Inventory', these are the IPIP-HEXACO scales (Ashton, Lee & Goldberg 2007), NOT the HEXACO-PI-R: all 40 item stems match ipip.ori.org/newhexaco_pi_key.htm's Forgiveness/Gentleness/Flexibility/Patience keys verbatim once the codebook's 'I ' prefix is removed (40/40), and the dataset's own listing calls it 'the IPIP HEXACO equivalent scales'. Within-facet numbering follows the IPIP key's order (+keyed first), and live-data polarity agrees item by item: + items correlate +0.59..+0.85 and - items -0.14..-0.80 with their facet's +keyed composite (e.g. AForg1..4 +0.63..+0.81, AForg5..10 -0.30..-0.61; APati1..5 +0.69..+0.85, APati6..10 -0.52..-0.80), so the stored data are raw, not reverse-scored. RIGHTS: register row HEXACO-PI-R (block, irw#1945) does not apply -- a name lead, not this instrument; its match_item_code ^hexaco does not match these codes. The IPIP-HEXACO wording originates on ipip.ori.org, so hexaco.org's non-commercial clause for the HEXACO-PI-R forms does not reach it. No new register row written. TEXT: item_text is the codebook sentence verbatim, including its mechanical 'I ' prefix; AFlex3 therefore ships as the ungrammatical 'I when interacting with a group of people, am often bothered by at least one of them.' (IPIP: 'When interacting with a group of people, am often bothered by at least one of them.') -- left as the codebook prints it, since that is the best evidence of what the online form showed. ANCHORS: codebook header gives '1 = strongly disagree, 2 = disagree, 3 = slightly disagree, 4 = neutral, 5 = slightly disagree, 6 = agree, 7 = strongly agree'; 5 is an evident typo (it duplicates 3 on a symmetric 7-point scale) and ships CORRECTED as 'slightly agree'. The original test page (openpsychometrics.org/tests/HEXACO/) now 404s and the Wayback Machine was offline, so the displayed label could not be confirmed. Casing of the anchors kept lowercase as printed. instructions blank: the codebook's lead sentence is a description of the rating scale for data users, not participant instructions. Raw 0 (unanswered) is recoded to NA by the script; 24 NA rows in the live table; every item uses all seven levels 1-7.
